# Purpose

This notebook turns the raw survey file into one tidy dataset that every later notebook reads. It applies the decisions logged at the end of `01_eda.qmd`, and nothing else: raw data is never modified, and the output is written to `data/processed/`.

Judgment calls are collected in one place (see **Decisions** below) so the team can review and change them.

```{r}
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
source("../R/load_data.R")

raw_data <- load_coupon_data()
problems(raw_data)   # should be empty
```

```{r}
n_raw <- nrow(raw_data)
cat("Raw data:", n_raw, "rows,", ncol(raw_data), "columns\n")
```

# Decisions (edit here)

```{r}
# Habit columns have ~1-2% missing each (605 rows, 4.8%, have at least one).
#   "drop" = remove those rows (default; keeps habits as clean ordered factors)
#   "keep" = leave them as NA and handle in modelling
habit_na_strategy <- "drop"
```

# 1. Remove columns with no information

Each drop is backed by a check, so the notebook fails loudly if the data ever changes.

```{r}
# toCoupon_GEQ5min: same value in every row
stopifnot(n_distinct(raw_data$toCoupon_GEQ5min) == 1)

# direction_opp is the exact opposite of direction_same
stopifnot(all(raw_data$direction_same + raw_data$direction_opp == 1))

# distance flags are nested: > 25 min implies > 15 min
stopifnot(!any(raw_data$toCoupon_GEQ25min == 1 & raw_data$toCoupon_GEQ15min == 0))

# car: almost entirely empty
cat("car is missing in", scales::percent(mean(is.na(raw_data$car)), accuracy = 0.1), "of rows\n")
```

# 2. Combine the geospatial flags into readable variables

The three nested distance flags (the always-1 `GEQ5min` plus `GEQ15min` and `GEQ25min`) become one ordered `distance`. The two direction flags become one `direction`. Nothing is lost.

```{r}
clean <- raw_data |>
  mutate(
    distance = case_when(
      toCoupon_GEQ25min == 1 ~ "Over 25 min",
      toCoupon_GEQ15min == 1 ~ "15-25 min",
      TRUE                   ~ "5-15 min"
    ) |> factor(levels = c("5-15 min", "15-25 min", "Over 25 min"), ordered = TRUE),
    direction = factor(if_else(direction_same == 1, "Same direction", "Opposite direction"),
                       levels = c("Same direction", "Opposite direction"))
  ) |>
  select(-car, -toCoupon_GEQ5min, -toCoupon_GEQ15min, -toCoupon_GEQ25min,
         -direction_same, -direction_opp)

count(clean, distance)
count(clean, direction)
```

# 3. Rename columns and relabel levels

Column names move to one style (`snake_case`, `passanger` typo fixed). Compact codes become readable labels, with the same wording used in the EDA charts. Ordered factors stay ordered.

```{r}
habit_levels <- c("never", "less1", "1~3", "4~8", "gt8")
habit_labels <- c("Never", "Less than 1", "1-3", "4-8", "More than 8")

clean <- clean |>
  rename(
    passenger             = passanger,
    marital_status        = maritalStatus,
    bar_freq              = Bar,
    coffee_house_freq     = CoffeeHouse,
    carry_away_freq       = CarryAway,
    restaurant_lt20_freq  = RestaurantLessThan20,
    restaurant_20_50_freq = Restaurant20To50
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # unordered
    coupon = fct_recode(coupon,
                        "Take-away"              = "Carry out & Take away",
                        "Restaurant (under $20)" = "Restaurant(<20)",
                        "Restaurant ($20-50)"    = "Restaurant(20-50)"),
    has_children = factor(has_children, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),

    # ordered
    expiration = factor(expiration, levels = c("2h", "1d"),
                        labels = c("2 hours", "1 day"), ordered = TRUE),
    age = factor(age,
                 levels = c("below21", "21", "26", "31", "36", "41", "46", "50plus"),
                 labels = c("Under 21", "21-25", "26-30", "31-35", "36-40", "41-45", "46-49", "50+"),
                 ordered = TRUE),
    across(ends_with("_freq"),
           \(x) factor(x, levels = habit_levels, labels = habit_labels, ordered = TRUE))
  )

glimpse(clean)
```

# 4. Respondent proxy ID

The file has no respondent ID, but each person appears in many rows (about 20). Rows from the same person are not independent, so a random row-level train/test split would leak. We build a proxy ID from the respondent-level columns (demographics plus habits), computed **before** any rows are dropped. If two real people share an identical profile they get the same ID, which is the safe direction for grouped splitting.

> `respondent_id` is only for grouping or splitting. Never use it as a predictor.

```{r}
clean <- clean |>
  group_by(across(c(gender, age, marital_status, has_children, education,
                    occupation, income, ends_with("_freq")))) |>
  mutate(respondent_id = cur_group_id()) |>
  ungroup()

cat("Distinct respondent profiles:", n_distinct(clean$respondent_id), "\n")
```

# 5. Missing habit values

See the missingness section of `01_eda.qmd`. Only a small share of rows is affected and a missing habit cannot be reliably imputed, so the default is to drop those rows. Missing values also look mildly related to acceptance (for example, rows with `Bar` missing accepted at about 51% vs 57% otherwise), so the dropped share is reported below, and the strategy is a one-line switch at the top if the team wants a sensitivity check.

```{r}
n_before <- nrow(clean)

if (habit_na_strategy == "drop") {
  clean <- clean |> drop_na(ends_with("_freq"))
}

cat("Habit NA strategy:", habit_na_strategy, "\n",
    "Rows removed:", n_before - nrow(clean),
    scales::percent((n_before - nrow(clean)) / n_before, accuracy = 0.1, prefix = "("),
    ")\n")
```

# 6. Duplicates

There is no respondent ID, so two identical rows could be two different people with the same profile answering the same scenario. We keep them and report the count.

```{r}
cat("Fully duplicated rows kept:", sum(duplicated(clean)), "\n")
```

# 7. Validate and save

```{r}
stopifnot(
  all(clean$Y %in% 0:1),
  is.ordered(clean$time), is.ordered(clean$age), is.ordered(clean$income),
  is.ordered(clean$education), is.ordered(clean$expiration), is.ordered(clean$distance),
  is.ordered(clean$bar_freq),
  !any(c("car", "toCoupon_GEQ5min", "passanger") %in% names(clean))
)
if (habit_na_strategy == "drop") stopifnot(sum(is.na(clean)) == 0)

cat("Clean data:", nrow(clean), "rows,", ncol(clean), "columns\n",
    "Acceptance rate:", scales::percent(mean(clean$Y), accuracy = 0.1), "\n")
```

Saved as `.rds` rather than `.csv` so the factor types and level order survive.

```{r}
dir.create("../data/processed", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
write_rds(clean, "../data/processed/coupon_clean.rds")
```

# Summary of changes

| Step | Change |
|---|---|
| Drop | `car` (99% missing), `toCoupon_GEQ5min` (constant), the raw distance and direction flags |
| Create | `distance` (ordered), `direction`, `respondent_id` (proxy) |
| Rename | `passanger` to `passenger`, camelCase to `snake_case`, habit columns end in `_freq` |
| Relabel | coupon names, `expiration`, `age`, habit bands, `has_children` |
| Rows | Habit NAs dropped (default); duplicates kept |
| Output | `data/processed/coupon_clean.rds` |

Not done here, on purpose: collapsing rare `occupation` levels, encoding for models, and train/test splitting. Those belong in a feature-engineering or modelling notebook.
